_README: Real published headlines, human-written, collected from design publications.
Two purposes: filling frame exemplar arrays, and serving as the discriminator's held-out set.
DO NOT add generated headlines to this file. DO NOT invent entries.
Every line appeared as a published article title.
Supplied by the project owner. Sources: Dezeen, Dwell, Remodelista, Architectural Digest.
v2: the first version was majority Dezeen, whose house grammar puts the studio name in
subject position, leaving only five entries that were agent-free and single-project. v2 adds
Dwell and Remodelista, both of which write agent-free by default.
Note the path: the phase brief referred to docs/fixtures/headline-corpus.md, which has never
existed. The corpus has lived here since it was first supplied.

_collectorNotes: Verbs are physical actions. Clads, perches, inserts, hides, frames, divides, riffs, fills,
turns, blends, pairs. Never features, showcases, elevates, transforms as an abstraction.
Evaluation is borrowed, not asserted. Where evaluative language appears it usually sits inside
quotation marks and belongs to a named person. Dwell is the exception and uses mild evaluative
adjectives directly (charming, stunning, cozy), which is worth noting as a divergence rather
A locative tail closes most of them.
Length runs past ten words routinely. Several entries run 12 to 16 words. The colon
constructions in particular need the room.
Agent-free is a house style, not a constraint. Dwell and Remodelista almost never lead with a
studio name and still produce headlines that read as important.
_humanSelection: `human` is what scripts/check-headline-discriminator.ts reads. A SUBSET of
byArrangement, chosen so the comparison is like-for-like.
v2 + the B8 rule changes took this from 5 to 26 — above the 20 the script
recommends, where v1 was below its floor of 5.
Two exclusions remain, and one that DROPPED OUT:
DROPPED: 'opens on a named agent'. It removed 57% of v1. B8 unbanned naming, so
agent-led headlines are now something Folio can produce and belong in the set.
1. Fails a Folio check - 4 use a banned generic verb, 5 a banned shape, 1 is over
the new 16-word cap, and 38 read as Title Case.
2. A different task - corpus-scope round-ups and news items.
THE TITLE CASE PROBLEM, unresolved. 38 of 80 entries are Title Case, because that
is Dwell and Remodelista house style; Folio's is sentence case. Excluding them
costs the whole project-as-subject group, which is otherwise the closest match to
what Folio produces. Ignoring casing instead would give 56 rather than 26, but the
judge could then separate on casing alone. 26 is the set that needs no
